findings.claim: A corridor side wall is drawn as a perspective-tapering SURFACE across consecutive perspective slots. For a surface spanning perspective slots [s..e] on the LEFT, slot p emits the ceiling PAIR { (134-4·(p-s)) + p, (134-4·(p-s-1)) + p } (drop the 2nd term at the near slot p=s); RIGHT mirror emits { 138+p, 142+p } at the body slots, { 138+p } at p=s. (Plus the floor twin +28 — the engine emits both bands.) The LADDER ARITHMETIC is PINNED: v1's LEFT surface (s=0,e=1) == captured {134 (p0), 131,135 (p1)} byte-exact; RIGHT == {138, 139,143} byte-exact. v2's surface anchors at s=2 (same ladder shifted); v5's LEFT tapers across all 4 slots (s=0,e=3) with a special deepest base (34) at p3.

LEFT) keyed to the perspective scale (the destRow band). The bases ARE the wall_emit_corner corner-family bases (maze-index-arithmetic call_sites corner_L 0x4e24: 7/4/15/19/83/87/106/114/...; the 130/134/138/142 are the wall_emit_quad side-emit family). The v5 p3 base 34 (vs the ladder's 122) is the special deepest-taper substitution — a documented sub-residue.

findings.claim: The side-wall SURFACE extent is NOT capped by the front OCCLUSION stop (computeVisibleDepths). v5's occlusion stop is depth 1 (solid front), yet its LEFT side-wall surface renders all FOUR perspective slots (the wall recedes past the cap). This is the 'a single family-base fires at MULTIPLE perspective depths' pattern the task flagged: the ceiling/floor occlusion (which depths get a center floor/ceiling) and the side-wall surface extent (how far a side wall tapers) are INDEPENDENT walks. The side-wall extent depends on the corridor's side-opening geometry (where side walls start/stop being solid), not on the front-edge profile alone — it is the engine's perspective ray-march, the decompiler-resistant residue.

evidence.details: v5 (lS[0,0,2,0] rS[0,2,2,2], occlusion stop d1) LEFT surface bases span p0..p3. v1 (lS[0,2,2,2], stop d2) LEFT surface spans only p0..p1. v2 (lS[0,2,0,2], stop none) LEFT surface anchored at p2..p3. So the build-depth counter [0x5040] is NOT live during a poked recompose (it reads 0 / stale at OR-blit time, and the gate bytes [0x5072..0x50a2] read recycled garbage). Recovering the LIVE wmaze relocated base via the span-store cseips also fails (no span stores fire). The unblock is a NAVIGATION-reach harness (walk the party to each target geometry from the 3-cell stub, arming the build watch on the genuine move) — but most parity-EVEN geometries are not navigable from the committed stub. trace-maze.ts `depthemit` is committed for the future navigation-driven trace.
